parsed.explanation: Combined regime pairs a highly protective state with an actively hostile federal layer the traveller cannot avoid. State law provides anti-discrimination, facility, housing, employment, bias-crime and traveller healthcare protections, but federal passport binary rules, document-discrepancy refusal and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, federal-facility exclusion, and documented federal-custody abuse remain operative. Local protections materially reduce street and service risk, but do not cancel federal entry, facility, detention or minor-care exposures.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal policy defines sex as binary at birth, stopped new X and birth-sex-mismatched passports, and was allowed by Supreme Court Nov 2025. Entry cable requires refusal where documents cast reasonable doubt, and consideration of permanent fraud ineligibility for wilful misrepresentation, never automatic.
entry_documents.protection: State documents allow surgery-free birth-certificate amendment, no doctor note for driver licence, and X/M/F markers. State anti-discrimination law covers public accommodations, housing and employment with a civil-rights complaint body.
entry_documents.interaction: State documents are separate from national passport/visa issuance. State openness does not govern federal border screening or federal document discrepancy handling.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections adopted conversion-therapy model including short haircuts, hormone removal and psychiatric substitution; reporting of trans prisoners stopped 2025. Immigration custody reports include forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of trans men.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. No federal custody protection is documented; state bias-crime and licensing protections do not apply to federal custody.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A document discrepancy or facilities incident can move a visitor into federal investigation or custody, where state protections do not operate.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with gender identity. Airport screening guidance notes invasive outing via secondary screening and pat-downs.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State law bars denial in places of public accommodation including hotels, restaurants, stores and transportation. Division is in most-protective tier; mapped state bathroom bans do not include this state in described groups.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State public-accommodation protection does not cancel federal facility restrictions in federal buildings or federally controlled spaces.

care_services.exposure: Federal orders and proposals restrict gender-affirming care for minors, bar public insurance reimbursement under 18 in proposed rules, and DOJ subpoenaed over 20 hospitals for under-19 patient records.
care_services.protection: April 2023 state order directs agencies to protect gender-affirming healthcare within state borders including people travelling from other jurisdictions. State hospital records must protect sexual orientation and gender identity data.
care_services.interaction: Effect of state order on out-of-state subpoenas or warrants for state provider records is not documented. Federal minor-care exposure persists for travelling families.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal executive orders remove gender-ideology materials, rescind pronoun policies, freeze funding, ban trans athletes, and May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises groups described as radically pro-transgender. Reward memo uses radical gender ideology phrase but not as criterion.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State anti-discrimination law since 2006, bias-crime enhancements for gender identity, panic-defence ban passed unanimously, and FBI local data include gender X.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal threat-framing creates investigative and funding pressure, while state law provides local recourse; federal framing does not override state protections in state venues.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal policy bans trans athletes entering for women's sports, directs investigation and possible prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition including names/pronouns, and restricts minor care. Guardian travelling with trans minor faces entry, school and care scrutiny.
minors_guardians.protection: State school guidance supports names, pronouns, facilities and records by identity; athletics allowed by gender identity. State chief legal office sued three boards adopting parental-notification policies.
minors_guardians.interaction: Outcome of that suit and current status of notification policies not documented. Federal funding threats may pressure schools despite state guidance.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: National poll 2025 found 66% support birth-sex on documents and 69% support birth-sex sports assignment. Invastive screening and federal hostility increase outing and scrutiny risk.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State bias-motivated crimes carry enhanced penalties. 2026 killings dataset places state among safest per-capita for trans women, suggesting private violence does not track legal hostility nationally.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: State police and licensing protections may help locally, but federal agents and border officers operate under federal policy when screening or detaining.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport suit by civil-liberties union for seven plaintiffs and challenges to executive orders are unresolved; several orders enjoined. No state complaint or prosecution statistics located.
remedies_unknowns.protection: State civil-rights body can investigate and grant relief. Legal-aid FAQ explains passport and document rules. Courts have blocked several federal orders.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are split: state relief for state services, but federal entry and custody remedies are slow, contested, and do not prevent initial refusal, facility exclusion or detention.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in having routine federal entry exclusion for document mismatch with weak remedy at border, but lower severity than 0.35-A in overall outcome because state-level services, lodging, healthcare and anti-discrimination relief are documented and courts are actively hearing challenges; imprisonment is not the typical visitor outcome.

Similar: ward or facility placement by document marker causes delay and denial rather than certain imprisonment, with remedies that work unevenly. Here marker-based federal facility exclusion is broader and entry can be refused, but state healthcare protection for travellers is stronger than in 0.55-C.

Higher than this case: 0.75-C has passport recognition, brief detention, counsel and compensation. Here federal binary passport rule, possible lifetime fraud consideration, federal facility ban and documented federal custody abuse are more severe, despite state protections.

parsed.synthesis: Traveller encounters state protection in hotels, clinics, housing and state venues, where complaint and bias-crime machinery exist. The operative risk is at federal touchpoints: border document check, federal facilities, screening, and any detention, where binary sex rules, refusal and fraud-ineligibility consideration, and documented custody harm apply. For minors, federal care, sports and school-facilitation orders add exposure that state traveller-care protection partly mitigates but cannot fully displace. Crossing out of the state enters a materially harsher enforcement environment.
